name: Ceftriaxone
executiveSummary: 3rd-generation cephalosporin. Adult 1–2 g IV/IM every 24 h (meningitis up to 2 g every 12 h / 4 g/day). Pediatrics 50–75 mg/kg/day (severe/meningitis 100 mg/kg/day; max 2 g, CNS 4 g).
indications:
## Indications

- Sepsis, meningitis, respiratory, skin/soft-tissue, bone, and urinary infections due to susceptible organisms.
- Gonorrhea / STI prophylaxis (single IM dose per guideline).

## Precautions

- **Do not mix or coadminister with IV calcium** in neonates (fatal precipitation); in other ages separate lines/timing.
- Avoid in hyperbilirubinemic neonates (displaces bilirubin).
- Incompatible with vancomycin, fluconazole, and aminoglycosides in the same line.

> Adjust if CrCl < 10 mL/min with concomitant hepatic failure.

adulto.dose: Usual infections: **1–2 g IV or IM every 24 h**. Severe / meningitis: **2 g every 12 h** (max **4 g/day**). Surgical prophylaxis: **1–2 g** once. Gonorrhea (current guides): **500 mg IM** once (adjust per CDC/local).
adulto.administration: IV: reconstitute with sterile water; dilute in 50–100 mL NS/5% dextrose; 30–60 min (or slow push 2–4 min by brand). IM: ≤ 1 g per site; 1% lidocaine without epinephrine reduces pain (IM only).
adulto.notes: No more than 1 g per IM injection.

pediatrico.dose: Mild–moderate: **50–75 mg/kg/day every 24 h**. Severe / sepsis / meningitis / neutropenia: **100 mg/kg/day every 24 h** (or divide q12h for CNS). Max **2 g/day** (CNS **4 g/day** in 2 doses). STI: **250 mg IM** once (children); adolescents as adult.
pediatrico.notes: Dose by weight. Confirm pneumococcal susceptibility in meningitis.

neonatal.dose: Orientative: **50 mg/kg every 24 h** (meningitis: specific NNU schemes). Prefer alternatives if bilirubin/IV calcium risk.
neonatal.notes: Contraindicated with concurrent IV calcium; wait per protocol (≥ 48 h in many centers after last dose).

stability:
## Stability

- Reconstituted/diluted: per label (usually hours at room temp / refrigerated).
- Protect from light by brand.
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Diarrhea, rash, eosinophilia, elevated liver enzymes, biliary sludge/lithiasis, candidiasis. Anaphylaxis in beta-lactam–allergic patients.
